text: Donald Davidson defended a strong 'linguistic requirement' on thought. What did he argue?
choices: To have beliefs at all one must have language, because having beliefs requires the concept of belief (including beliefs about others' beliefs), and the resources for that are linguistic
Natural language is merely the expression of a prior, innate Mentalese
Pre-linguistic infants and many animals clearly possess full propositional thought
Thought is fundamentally imagistic and spatial rather than linguistic
explanation: Davidson tied genuine propositional attitudes to possessing the concept of belief, which he held requires language -- a view the book flags as controversial for seeming to deny thought to infants and animals. Option 2 is the opposing view (and the standard objection to Davidson); option 1 is Fodor's LOT; option 3 is the imagistic/nonverbal-thought position.
